sentences.text:
The brief facts of the case is that the petitioner lodged a complaint before the Dispur Police Station being Dispur Police Station Case No. 1769/2022 against the accused person named therein thereby stating that the petitioner/informant is the owner and proprietor of M/s Rejuve Aesthetics,
a cosmetology clinic and she is a collaboration partner with DHI brand through their master franchisee being Silver Maple Healthcare Services Pvt. Ltd.

entities.text: Silver Maple Healthcare Services Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioner/informant further stated in her complaint that she took the franchisee of DHI brand in the month of August, 2015 and then she came into contact with the accused person namely Mr. Ajay Bansal who is the Director and CEO of the said Company.

Mr. Ajay Bansal, holding the position of the CEO of the company befriended with the petitioner/informant and on that pretext he began to frequently call her and then started sharing personal information about his past relationships.

It was further stated in the Complaint that the accused person took advantage of the petitioner/informant's trust and given his position of authority within the company, the petitioner/informant fell prey to his predatory practices.

It was only after few months of their interaction, the petitioner/informant realized that the accused person is a known predator and a sexual offender and many women employees have fallen prey to his tactics.

It was further stated that the accused person would contact her at late hours in the night after getting drunk and used to harass her telling her that he was in love with her and wanted to have sex with her and each time she refused, he had threatened to terminate her clinic and destroy her future since he has all the power, money and influence.

Moreover, on 16 June, 2022, the accused person established contact with the petitioner/informant and threatened her that he would terminate the collaboration agreement if she does not extend him sexual favours.
Page No.# 3/5 4.

Mr. N.N.B. Choudhury, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that earlier the Investigating Officer on 18.07.2023 submitted a Final Report i.e. FR No. 1861 and accordingly, the petitioner filed an objection before the jurisdictional Magistrate Court with a prayer to take cognizance and direct the Investigating Officer for further investigation by appointing a new Investigating Officer.

5. Mr. N.N.B. Choudhury, learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that though investigation was carried out, however, the Investigating Officer yet again submitted the Final Report vide No. 4175/2024 dated 28.07.2022, which was accepted by the Magistrate Court by Order dated 04.03.2025.
Situated thus, the present petition has been filed.

6. The Order dated 10.08.2023 passed by the Magistrate Court in the said petition filed by the petitioner is reproduced hereunder for ready reference:-
"Today is the date fixed for necessary order.
I have already heard learned counsel for the informant.
It is submitted inter alia

sentences.text: 2 matter in the right direction and has come to an erroneous decision by filing final form in the instant case.
The informant/victim in her statement recorded u/s 164 of C.rPC, has categorically stated that she had never consented to the sexual act committed by the accused person.
However, the I/O, as per section 114-A of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, ought to 1872, ought to have filed chargesheet instead of final report.
I have perused the case record as well as the case diary.

It appears from the statement of the victim/informant u/s 164 of Cr.P.C., that there are sufficient incriminating materials against the accused person namely Ajay Bansal and situated thus, this Court is of the opinion that the investigation of this case is not proper and suffers from lapses.
As such, there is scope for further investigation in this case and thus this Court deems it fit to reject the final report.
The O/C of Dispur P.S to conduct further investigation into the allegations against the accused person by entrusting a different I/O and to submit the Final Form at the earliest.
Send back the CD to O/C Dispur P.S. Inform the O/C. Office to take step.
Accordingly the petition no. 1660 is disposed of."

7. Upon perusing of the aforesaid order, it appears that the Magistrate Court being satisfied from the statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 of CrPC that there are sufficient incriminating materials available against the accused, observed Page No.# 4/5 that the investigation of the case is not done properly and suffered from lapses.

Accordingly, the Magistrate Court rejected the said FR and directed the O.C. of the jurisdictional Police Station to further investigate into the allegations against the accused persons by entrusting a different Investigating Officer to submit the final report at the earliest.
8.

Apt also to reproduce the relevant paragraph of the Order dated 04.03.2025, which is reproduced hereunder for ready reference:-
"15.

So far as the other allegations under Sections 509, 354A(1)(i), 354(D), 427, 420,
109 and 341 of IPC are concerned, the I.O has categorically stated that during investigation he could hardly gather any material that substantiates the ingredients of the aforesaid offences.

The I.O has further stated that the petitioner/victim failed to provide him with the footages of the alleged assault, threat or wrongful confinement despite CCTV cameras being installed at the place of occurrence."
9.

Upon perusing of the aforesaid order, it appears that the Investigating Officer has categorically stated during investigation that he could hardly gathered any material that substantiate the ingredients under Section 509, 354A(1)(i), 354(D), 427, 420, 109 and 341 of IPC and that the petitioner/victim failed to provide him with the footages and alleged assault, threat or wrongful confinement despite CCTV cameras being installed at the place of occurrence i.e. Hotel RADISSON BLUE RESORT, Goa.

11. Before further proceeding into the matter, this Court deems appropriate to call for the record of Dispur Police Station Case No. 1769/2022.

12. Mr. P.S. Lahkar, learned Addl. Public Prosecutor shall accordingly produce the case record from the jurisdictional Police Station on the next date of listing.
